subject: Dedicated pool degraded throughput — customer checklist & mitigation
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme-retail.com; samantha.lee@acme-retail.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool degraded throughput — immediate checklist

Hi Samantha / Acme Ops team,

We observed a sustained throughput degradation in your dedicated GPU pool starting ~08:45 PDT this morning. The impact is increased token latency for your live scoring endpoint and occasional timeouts at peak concurrency. We have temporarily limited burst allocation to the pool while investigating the root cause.

Immediate actions we've taken (already applied):
- Paused non-critical batch jobs linked to your tenant (to free headroom)
- Enforced low-priority throttling on background routes
- Enabled conservative autoscale policy (target headroom = 15%)

Suggested customer-side checklist (what helps fast recovery):
- If possible, reduce max concurrent requests briefly during 09:00–11:00 PDT
- Switch critical routes to your fallback model (gpt-small-fallback) — instructions below
- Share any unusual traffic patterns or large model warmups that started at ~08:30

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (live metrics snapshot), mitigation_checklist.txt (steps to flip routing)

We know any disruption is costly — we’ll keep you updated every 60–90 minutes and follow with a post-incident writeup and proposed remediation credits.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Acme Ops <ops@acme-retail.com>

Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 09:28:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool degraded throughput — immediate checklist

Thanks Mina — we see the spike on our side too.

Quick Qs:
- Where do we flip to the fallback model? We have multiple routes (pricing engine + search ranking).
- Any ETA on when the warm nodes will be back?

We can temporarily throttle the pricing engine; we prefer not to throttle search ranking if possible.

—Samantha

ops@acme-retail.com

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated pool degraded throughput — action items (internal)

Marissa / Ben — FYI and please action. Acme is live and sensitive to latency increases. Priorities:
1) Spin extra warm nodes in us-west-2 for this dedicated pool and allow limited overcommit for 60m (route-specific)
2) Apply fast fallback routing: pricing engine -> gpt-small-fallback; search ranking remain on main but with reduced concurrency where possible
3) Prepare credit proposal (1–2 days of billed tokens backstop) if service window extends beyond 6 hours
4) I'll coordinate customer comms; schedule a postmortem link by end of day tomorrow

Internal notes: autoscaler logs show a late sensor read that underreported queue pressure (likely telemetry lag). Ben — can you pull the autoscaler debug trace and share? Soojin — can you draft the talking points for the customer call?

Thanks — Mina

Date: Tue, 03 Jul 2028 12:10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool degraded throughput — mitigation update

Samantha / Acme team — update from ops: we've spun two warm nodes in us-west-2 and temporarily allowed 10% overcommit for your pool. Pricing engine is now routed to gpt-small-fallback for write operations; this cut average p50 token latency by ~18% in our staged checks.

What we still need from Acme:
- Confirm you can throttle pricing engine concurrency by 20% for the next 90 minutes (helps avoid oscillation)
- Share any large concurrent batch runs scheduled for the next 12 hours

Next steps:
- We’ll continue to monitor and will attempt an autoscaler recalibration at 14:00 PDT once telemetry catch-up completes.
- I’m drafting a short postmortem and will share a first-pass doc tomorrow EOD.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme-retail.com, samantha.lee@acme-retail.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — Dedicated pool event (Jul 3)

Hi Samantha / Acme team — thank you for your patience. Here is a short summary and action agenda:

Summary (what happened)
- 08:30–08:45 PDT: a telemetry lag caused the autoscaler to underreport queue pressure for your dedicated pool during a sudden concurrency ramp.
- 08:45–11:30 PDT: degraded throughput and elevated token latency; limited burst capacity applied at 08:50 while mitigations executed.
- 09:12–12:30 PDT: temporary routing changes and warm nodes reduced latency; service returned to expected levels by ~12:30.

Immediate remediation we applied
- Temporary fallback routing for pricing engine to gpt-small-fallback
- Warm nodes spun up and limited overcommit enabled for 75 minutes
- Autoscaler sensor calibration scheduled and completed 07/04 14:00 PDT

Customer impact & credit proposal
- Impact window ~3h45m with intermittent elevated latency; limited timeouts at peak.
- Proposed credit: one week of net billed tokens for the affected pool (applied as account credit) — we can discuss on the call.

Action items
- [Redwood] Root cause analysis and postmortem doc (link below) — draft published.
- [Redwood] Autoscaler telemetry fix deployed to staging; rollout to prod scheduled for next maintenance window.
- [Acme] Confirm acceptance of the temporary routing changes and credit offer
- [Joint] 30-minute follow-up call to review postmortem and longer-term changes (propose Thu 07/05 10:00 PDT)

Postmortem (draft): https://redwood.company/confluence/dedicated-pool-2028-07-03-postmortem
HubSpot record: https://hubspot.redwood/deals/ACME-4219

If you’d like a more detailed timeline or extra telemetry slices, we can attach them to the Confluence post.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
